A.explanation: Net p.d. of $500\text{ V}$ over $0.20\text{ m}$ gives $a \approx 2.4 \times 10^{11} \text{ m s}^{-2}$ and the proton is pushed away from the $800\text{ V}$ top plate downwards.

B.explanation: Magnitude $2.4 \times 10^{11} \text{ m s}^{-2}$ is correct for $500\text{ V}$, but a positive proton moves from high to low potential so it cannot accelerate upwards toward the $800\text{ V}$ plate.

C.explanation: Direction downwards is correct, but $5.3 \times 10^{11} \text{ m s}^{-2}$ uses $1100\text{ V}$ from adding $800\text{ V}$ and $300\text{ V}$ instead of the difference $500\text{ V}$.

D.explanation: This combines both errors: it uses $1100\text{ V}$ instead of $500\text{ V}$ and gives upwards motion toward higher potential for a positive charge.

hints: Notice the top plate is at $800\text{ V}$ and the bottom plate is at $300\text{ V}$ with separation $20\text{ cm} = 0.20\text{ m}$ - what is the potential difference actually across the gap?
Recall the uniform field strength is $E = V/d$ directed from high potential to low potential - which way does this point between the plates?
Connect force to acceleration for the proton using $F = qE$ and $a = F/m$ with $q = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$ and $m = 1.67 \times 10^{-27} \text{ kg}$.
walkthrough: Find the p.d. between the plates. Both + terminals connect to the plates, so $V = 800 - 300 = 500\text{ V}$ across $d = 20\text{ cm} = 0.20\text{ m}$.

Find field strength and direction. $E = V/d = 500/0.20 = 2500\text{ V m}^{-1}$. Field points from high to low potential, so from the top $800\text{ V}$ plate to the bottom $300\text{ V}$ plate, i.e. downwards.
Find electric force on the proton. $F = qE = (1.6 \times 10^{-19}) \times 2500 = 4.0 \times 10^{-16}\text{ N}$ downwards, since positive charge follows the field.
Find acceleration using Newton's second law. $a = F/m = 4.0 \times 10^{-16} / 1.67 \times 10^{-27} \approx 2.4 \times 10^{11} \text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Direction is the same as the force on a positive charge, downwards. This is option A.
